youtube.title: Why Bridges Have Gaps in the Road 🌉 #Shorts #science #facts #didyouknow
youtube.description:
The thumping seam you feel when driving onto a bridge is an expansion joint. Steel and concrete expand when heated and shrink when cooled, and a long bridge can change length by many centimeters between winter and summer. Without a gap, the expanding steel would push against itself with enormous force and make the road buckle. Expansion joints give the bridge room to grow and shrink safely.
